speaker_role: current admissions officer (Harvard College admissions committee member hosting the video), plus a real Harvard alumni interviewer and a current Harvard student in the mock interview
commercial_incentive: None evident; official Harvard admissions office video.
key_insights: Alumni interviews are assigned at the admissions committee's discretion based on local alumni availability; not every applicant gets one, and lacking an interview does not disadvantage the application.
The applicant does not initiate contact; the assigned alumni interviewer reaches out first, typically by email, so applicants should check email regularly during the cycle.

Interviewers only receive the applicant's name, high school, and contact info -- no essays, recommendations, or activity lists -- so it's a blank-slate conversation, not a follow-up on written materials.

The modeled interview covers open-ended questions: what you want from college, your high school experience, a formative extracurricular/passion project, how friends would describe you, a proud accomplishment, and a challenge overcome.

The mock interviewee's strongest material came from a detailed personal project she could speak to specifically and reflectively, illustrating the kind of concrete, story-driven answer that resonates.
Applicants should prepare a few thoughtful questions to ask their interviewer, since the conversation ends with time for the applicant to ask about the interviewer's own college experience.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Interviewer notes the mock interview is meant to run about 45 minutes to an hour.
notable_or_distinctive: An official, unscripted-feeling live demonstration of a full alumni interview exchange from a top-tier school, rather than tips presented abstractly.
reliability_notes: Official first-party Harvard content, so reliable for Harvard's own process specifically; other schools' alumni interview logistics may differ.
